important.name: Documented harness boundary omits harness_lib.project, which arc-straps imports
important.summary:
CLAUDE.md:12-14 says arc-straps reaches harness only through harness-skill-api, harness_lib.config and harness_lib.plugin_config, and plugins/arc-straps/README.md:40-47 repeats the closed list. In the same PR, arc_meta_config.py:10 imports harness_lib.project.project_root and paths() calls it at line 37, so a subfolder repo resolves to its project (test_a_subfolder_reads_the_project_config depends on this). A harness change to project_root would break arc-straps while both boundary documents say it cannot.

Also (docs): CLAUDE.md:16-18 and plugins/arc-straps/README.md:82-84 say a new arc-straps key touches defaults.json, the schema, `ArcMetaPaths` and `paths()` in arc_meta_config.py, and the README table. The shipped module also type-checks keys in `_meta` with the `_OPTIONAL` tuple (arc_meta_config.py:16,48-58). Without jsonschema, that check is the only type validation. A key added by following the list gets no fallback type check, and `paths()` can fail with a raw TypeError on a non-string value instead of a ConfigError.

Also (system_shape): CLAUDE.md:15-17 and plugins/arc-straps/README.md:82-84 list the places a new arc-straps key touches: defaults.json, the schema, ArcMetaPaths and paths(), and the README table. The type checks that run without jsonschema live in a separate function, _meta() with its _OPTIONAL tuple (arc_meta_config.py:16,49-59). A key added only in the listed places gets no type check on a load without jsonschema.
fix: Add `harness_lib.project` (`project_root`) to the boundary list in CLAUDE.md:12-14 and to the bullet list in plugins/arc-straps/README.md:45-47.

Alternatively, drop the import and have paths() resolve the root through an API the documents already name (for example a load_config path that walks up to the project), keeping test_a_subfolder_reads_the_project_config green.
Add '`_meta` (and `_OPTIONAL` for a nullable path)' to the touch list in both CLAUDE.md and the plugin README Configuration paragraph.
Name `_meta()` (and `_OPTIONAL`) beside `ArcMetaPaths` and `paths()` in CLAUDE.md:15-17 and plugins/arc-straps/README.md:82-84.

important.name: Plugin README says toolbox-level help is checked, but no check reads it
important.summary:
plugins/arc-straps/README.md:10-11 lists the toolbox-level help among the surfaces checked against the canonical XML by check_canonical/check_applied/entry_sources. All three are per-tool: none reads toolbox.content.rc, toolbox.metadata.xml or the toolbox_source. The update guidance at README.md:91-92 ('sweep check_applied over tool_names() and apply the tools it flags') therefore misses the toolbox page. That page's idAbs and useLimit are rendered by the same generator (mf.to_pro_html, arc_meta_toolbox.py:137,143), so a generator update leaves it stale and nothing flags it. The SKILL.md generator-change scoping rule (:57-65) has the same blind spot.

Also (docs): plugins/arc-straps/README.md:88-89 says an apply rewrites the archive 'after copying it to <archive>.bak', then validates. `arc_meta_archive.rewrite` (arc_meta_archive.py:69-72) writes and validates the temp copy first and takes the backup only after validation passes. A failed apply therefore leaves any older .bak untouched, which is not what the README implies. The repo README row (README.md:40) has the same ordering.

Also (overall): plugins/arc-straps/README.md:10-11 says the read-only check compares 'the archive's hover text, "?" page and toolbox-level help against that XML (check_canonical, check_applied, entry_sources)'. arc_meta_api reads only per-tool members (<Tool>.tool/...). Nothing compares toolbox.content.rc or toolbox.metadata.xml with toolbox_source; only apply_toolbox's dry run reports toolbox drift.
fix: Correct plugins/arc-straps/README.md:10-11 so toolbox-level help appears under Apply only. Extend README.md:91-92 and the SKILL.md generator-change rule with 'then dry-run apply_toolbox; apply it when it does not report UNCHANGED'.
Or add a read-only toolbox check to arc_meta_api (comparing the archive against build_rc/build_metadata of the configured toolbox_source) and keep the README claim.

Reword to: 'An apply writes a temp copy, validates it, then copies the original to `<archive>.bak` and swaps the copy in; a failed validation leaves the archive and any older `.bak` unchanged.' Apply the same order in README.md:40.
Drop 'and toolbox-level help' from the Check bullet, and add that toolbox-level drift shows in the apply_toolbox dry run (UNCHANGED vs DRY-RUN).
Add a check_toolbox call to arc_meta_api that compares the archive with build_rc/build_metadata, and list it in SKILL.md's API table.

important.name: rc writer treats any description as wired; check_applied keeps reporting hover_unwired
important.summary:
check_applied (_hover_problem) and ParamRow.hover_wired count a surface as wired only when tool.content holds exactly "$rc:<key>". The rc writer's missing_refs wires a parameter only when "description" is absent from it, and the summary only when "description" is absent from tool.content. A tool.content whose description is a literal string or another $rc: key is never rewired: apply_rc reports "no changes (already matches canonical XML)", or _dangling says "tool.content references $rc:<key>, which the rc lacks", which is false, while check_applied reports hover_unwired on every run. The API docstring says the checker and the writers cannot drift, and here a writer cannot clear a defect the checker reports. The rc module docstring promises that a missing reference gets added, but a wrong reference is never fixed.

Also (overall): check_applied and apply_rc classify two rc states differently, so Step 5 of the skill ('check_applied prints clean for every tool changed') cannot be reached and no documented call fixes it. (1) Dangling reference: tool.content already holds "$rc:<key>" but the rc map lacks <key>. apply_rc deliberately leaves it out: _dangling only reports it, and _set adds a key only when it is in rc_map or in add_keys, which holds only missing_refs. check_applied then sees ref == $rc:key and actual None and reports hover_stale ('rc <key> differs from the canonical text'). The skill reads hover_stale as unpublished, unchecked text to leave out, which is the wrong diagnosis here. run_rc also returns changed=False although the archive differs from the canonical source, contradicting the ApplyOutcome.changed contract (arc_meta_models.py:110). (2) Literal description: a parameter or summary whose tool.content description is present but is not $rc:<key>. missing_refs skips it ('description' not in param is False), but _hover_problem reports hover_unwired. The skill says apply_rc 'wires every missing reference', yet every rerun leaves this hover_unwired. Both README claims that check_applied 'passes exactly when the archive holds what an apply writes' are false in these states.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md:60-62 and :107 say apply_rc wires every missing $rc: reference for every parameter with non-empty canonical text, Step 5 (:121) expects check_applied to print clean afterwards, and README.md:15-16 says a passing check_applied means the archive holds exactly what an apply writes. Two cases break this. (1) missing_refs (arc_meta_rc.py:52-58) only wires a summary or parameter that has no `description` key at all. A literal or mis-keyed description is left alone, but _hover_problem (arc_meta_api.py:284-286) reports hover_unwired for any ref other than `$rc:<key>`. (2) When tool.content already references a key the rc lacks, _dangling/_apply_to_rc (arc_meta_rc.py:102-105, 115-125) leave the key out on purpose and report 'no changes'. check_applied then reports hover_stale (arc_meta_api.py:287-288, since rc.get(key) is None). test_run_names_a_reference_the_rc_lacks_and_leaves_it_out pins that writer behavior, and the round-trip test covers neither case. An agent following the skill re-applies and gets the same problem every time.
fix: In missing_refs and _dangling, test param.get("description") != f"$rc:{key}" (and content.get(SUMMARY_KEY) != "$rc:description" for the summary) instead of key presence. Make wire_content replace an existing summary value in place (add_summary drops its `SUMMARY_KEY not in content` guard and the loop overwrites out[SUMMARY_KEY]). Update the rc module docstring to say that a missing or wrong reference is rewired.

Or keep the writer as it is and make _hover_problem report a separate code (for example hover_foreign_ref) for a description that is present but not the expected $rc: reference, with the rc report naming it, so the two surfaces agree that the writer leaves it alone.

Make apply_rc converge: pass the _dangling keys to _apply_to_rc as addable (and count them in changed), and wire a param or summary whose description is not $rc:<key>. Then add a roundtrip case per state to tests/arc/test_arc_meta_roundtrip.py and update test_run_names_a_reference_the_rc_lacks_and_leaves_it_out.

Keep the writer as is, but give each state its own ProblemCode in check_applied (for example hover_dangling, hover_literal) with a detail that names the remedy. Document the codes in SKILL.md (Rules, Step 5, API table), correct ApplyOutcome.changed or run_rc's changed value, and qualify the 'exactly when' sentence in both READMEs.

Make the writer converge on the checker: missing_refs treats any description other than f"$rc:{key}" as unwired, and run_rc passes the dangling keys into _apply_to_rc's add_keys. Add both cases to tests/arc/test_arc_meta_roundtrip.py.

Or keep the writer as ported and document the gap: SKILL.md Steps 4-5 and Judgment say that a 'which the rc lacks; not added' line or a literal description leaves hover_stale or hover_unwired that only a manual tool.content or rc edit clears and that goes in the reply. Narrow the 'exactly what an apply writes' claims in plugins/arc-straps/README.md:15-16 and README.md:34 to match.

minor.name: Plan pinned interfaces drift from shipped modules
minor.summary: The plan presents Sections 4.2 and 4.3 as pinned code, but the shipped modules differ. `_check` there rejects unknown keys unconditionally, while the shipped version rejects them only when the schema sets additionalProperties false (plugin_config.py:38-39). `paths()` there uses `load_config(Path(repo))` and `rstrip('/')`, while the shipped module resolves `project_root`, adds `_meta` type checks and an `_inside` outside-root refusal, and drops the rstrip. Every task checkbox is still `- [ ]`. A reader taking the plan as the reference for the config contract gets the wrong behavior.
fix: Add a one-line 'as built' note under Section 4 headings 4.2/4.3 pointing at the shipped modules and naming the differences, or update the pinned blocks to the shipped code.

minor.name: Plugin README misstates config validation without jsonschema
minor.summary:
plugins/arc-straps/README.md:56-58 says the schema refuses an absolute path only when jsonschema is importable and that without it `plugin_section` 'rejects unknown keys and nothing else'. The code does something else. `plugin_config._check` (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/plugin_config.py:38-41) rejects only top-level unknown keys, so a typo such as `arc_meta.atbxx` is silently ignored and the default is used. `arc_meta_config._meta` (arc_meta_config.py:48-58) type-checks every arc_meta key and `_inside` (:61-66) refuses any location outside the project root, `..` included, whether or not jsonschema is present. Neither check is documented. Line 30 also lists jsonschema as a requirement, which contradicts the optional behavior described at line 56.

Also (overall): plugins/arc-straps/README.md:56-58 says that without jsonschema 'plugin_section rejects unknown keys and nothing else'. plugin_config._check rejects only unknown top-level keys of the section, so arc_meta.nope passes unflagged. Meanwhile arc_meta_config._meta checks every path key's type and _inside refuses any path that resolves outside the project root (an absolute path included), so more than unknown keys is checked. The Requirements bullet (line 30-31) lists jsonschema as needed, which conflicts with the 'only when jsonschema is importable' fallback the same file describes.

Also (system_shape): plugins/arc-straps/README.md:56-58 says that without jsonschema, plugin_section rejects unknown keys and nothing else, and :30-31 lists jsonschema as required. In the code, plugin_config._check (plugin_config.py:38-42) rejects only unknown top-level keys, so a typo under arc_meta (for example `tooldir`) is silently ignored and the default is used. arc_meta_config._meta (:49-59) still checks the types, and _inside (:62-67) refuses any location that resolves outside the project root (including an absolute path elsewhere) whether or not jsonschema is installed. That refusal is not documented anywhere.
fix: Rewrite README lines 55-58: paths are relative to the project root and any location resolving outside it (absolute or `..`) is a config error; key types are checked on every load; with jsonschema the schema also refuses unknown keys at every level; without it only unknown top-level section keys are refused, so a mistyped `arc_meta` key falls back to its default. In line 30, mark jsonschema as optional (needed for full validation).

Reword line 56-58: without jsonschema, plugin_section rejects unknown top-level keys of the section; arc_meta_config still checks each key's type and refuses a location outside the project root; nested unknown keys and the relative-path pattern are checked only with jsonschema. In line 30-31, say jsonschema is optional.

Rewrite README.md:56-58 to match the code. Without jsonschema, unknown keys directly under plugins.arc-straps are refused, but unknown keys inside arc_meta are not; types are always checked; every resolved location must lie inside the project root. Say jsonschema is optional at :30-31.

minor.name: toolbox_source default name is ambiguous about the .atbx suffix
minor.summary: The schema says null means '<parent of tool_dir>/<archive file name>.xml'. The code (arc_meta_config.py:42) builds tool_dir.parent / f"{atbx.name}.xml", where atbx.name keeps its extension, so the default is 'Tools.atbx.xml', not 'Tools.xml'. The text is technically right, but 'archive file name' can easily be read as the stem. A project that keeps 'Tools.xml' would get a missing-file error at the default and would have to read the code to see why.
fix: Reword the toolbox_source description to '... null means <parent of tool_dir>/<archive file name, extension included>.xml (e.g. Tools.atbx.xml).' and make the same edit to the matching row in plugins/arc-straps/README.md:64.

minor.name: SKILL Step 4 implies DRY-RUN line means the rc would change
minor.summary: SKILL.md:86-90 says a dry run that would write ends with 'DRY-RUN: nothing written...', and that apply_rc reports `<Tool>: no changes` when there is nothing to write, so that apply is skipped. `run_rc` (arc_meta_rc.py:192-195) appends the DRY-RUN line on every dry run, including after '<Tool>: no changes (already matches canonical XML)'. A rc dry run with nothing to write therefore also ends with DRY-RUN. `run_page` and `run_toolbox` do return UP TO DATE/UNCHANGED without that line. An agent keying on the last line runs a needless (no-op) apply.
fix: Reword SKILL.md:86-90 so that for apply_rc the first line `<Tool>: no changes` decides, whatever the last line says.
Or make run_rc append the DRY-RUN line only when `replacements` is non-empty, matching the page and toolbox writers (add a test in tests/arc/test_arc_meta_rc.py).

minor.name: check_applied row omits what page_stale and page_style_stale cover
minor.summary:
SKILL.md:197 lists page_stale as text, a dropped or extra parameter, or a displayname/type/direction/datatype attribute. SKILL.md:165 says page_style_stale means the archive holds older markup. `check_applied` also reports page_stale for a missing tool.metadata.xml page and for a resTitle or keyword mismatch (arc_meta_api.py:390-403,420-421). It reports page_style_stale when the page's parameter order differs from the canonical order (:342-346), which can come from a canonical XML edit rather than a generator change. The Rules re-apply scoping (SKILL.md:56-65) reads these codes, so the gaps matter.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md:197 lists page_stale causes as text, a dropped or extra parameter, or the displayname/type/direction/datatype attributes. The code also reports page_stale for resTitle and keyword drift (arc_meta_api.py:390-403) and for a missing tool.metadata.xml (:420-421), and reports a parameter-order difference as page_style_stale (:342-346). The entry_sources row (:195) omits entry_exists and embedded_script, the two fields Step 2 (:76-79) branches on.
fix: Extend the SKILL.md:197 row: page_stale also covers a missing page, the resTitle and the keywords; page_style_stale also covers parameter order. Adjust SKILL.md:165 to 'older markup or parameter order'.

Extend the check_applied row with the resTitle/keywords/missing-page page_stale causes and the parameter-order page_style_stale cause, and add entry_exists and embedded_script to the entry_sources row.

minor.name: A malformed archive help page aborts check_applied instead of reading as page_stale
minor.summary: _page_problems runs _xml() on tool.metadata.xml, which raises ApiError when the page is not well-formed. The whole check_applied call then fails, and the hover results are lost too. The page writer treats the same unreadable page as changed so that the rewrite can repair it (_current_page docstring), and _shown_plain follows the same rule for archive-side text ("so that surface reads as stale instead of blaming the canonical XML"). Also, a page that parses but has no <tool> element is reported as "the archive holds no tool.metadata.xml help page", which is wrong because the member exists.
fix: In _page_problems, catch the ApiError from _xml (and an undecodable page from read_text) and return a PAGE_STALE problem such as "the archive help page is not well-formed XML; apply_page rewrites it". Use a separate detail, "the archive help page has no <tool> element", when page_root parses but page_tool is None.

minor.name: check_applied leaks raw zip errors for a corrupt illustration
minor.summary: The arc_meta_api module docstring says refusals raise ApiError. _archive_page reads tool.illustration.png with a bare zf.read(image), so a CRC-bad or non-inflating member raises zipfile.BadZipFile or zlib.error. Neither is a ValueError, so check_applied's ValueError wrapper does not catch them. arc_meta_page.read_illustration refuses the same member as an ApiError, so the checker and the writer disagree on the same archive defect.
fix: In _archive_page, catch (zipfile.BadZipFile, zlib.error) around zf.read(image) and raise ApiError(f"{image} in {p.atbx.name} is corrupt ({exc})"), or call arc_meta_page.read_illustration's logic through a shared helper in arc_meta_archive. Add a corrupt-illustration case to tests/arc/test_arc_meta_api.py.

minor.name: _link_target docstring promises a project-relative path but returns an absolute one outside the project
minor.summary: The docstring says the function returns "The project-relative module a tool.script.execute.link names". When the resolved link falls outside p.root, the ValueError branch returns joined.as_posix(), an absolute path. ToolSources.entry then holds an absolute machine path, and registry_stale compares it against a project-relative registry py_path, which always reads as stale.
fix: Make the docstring say it returns the project-relative path, or the absolute path when the link resolves outside the project. Alternatively, return None for an outside link (so registry_stale stays False) and document that choice.

minor.name: Corrupt archive members escape the check API as raw zipfile/zlib errors
minor.summary: read_text calls zf.read(name) and catches only UnicodeDecodeError, so a member that fails its CRC (zipfile.BadZipFile) or does not inflate (zlib.error) propagates unchanged. Neither is a ValueError, so check_applied's ValueError wrapper does not catch them either. arc_meta_api._archive_page also reads tool.illustration.png with a bare zf.read. arc_meta_page.read_illustration refuses the same member with an ApiError, and arc_meta_rc._read_tool catches both errors. The API module docstring says refusals raise ApiError. arc_meta_toolbox._current catches BadZipFile but not zlib.error.
fix: In arc_meta_archive.read_text, wrap zf.read(name) in `except (zipfile.BadZipFile, zlib.error) as exc: raise ApiError(f"{name} in {label} is corrupt ({exc})") from exc`. In arc_meta_api._archive_page, read the illustration through the same guarded path, for example by reusing arc_meta_page.read_illustration or a shared read_bytes helper in arc_meta_archive.

minor.name: Without jsonschema, unknown or empty arc_meta keys are accepted silently
minor.summary: plugin_section's fallback when jsonschema is missing checks only top-level unknown keys of the section. _meta checks only the value types. A typo such as "tooldir" or "atbx_path" under arc_meta is ignored and the default is used without warning. tool_dir "" (schema minLength 1) resolves to the project root. harness_lib.config._plugins explicitly checks its shape on a load without jsonschema, and _meta's docstring makes the same claim for path types, but nested unknown keys are not checked.
fix: In arc_meta_config._meta, refuse `set(meta) - {"atbx", "tool_dir", "toolbox_source", "registry"}` with a ConfigError naming the unknown keys, and refuse an empty string for tool_dir or any optional path.

minor.name: apply_rc dry run with nothing to write still ends in DRY-RUN
minor.summary:
SKILL.md Step 4 (lines 86-90) says a dry run that would write ends 'DRY-RUN: nothing written...'. When there is nothing to write, apply_rc reports '<Tool>: no changes' and the apply is skipped. run_rc appends the DRY-RUN line whenever apply is False, including when replacements is empty. So a no-change dry run also ends in DRY-RUN, which by the skill's own rule means 'would write'. apply_page (UP TO DATE) and apply_toolbox (UNCHANGED) both return early without the DRY-RUN line.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md:86-90 says a dry run that would write ends with 'DRY-RUN: nothing written...', and that with nothing to write apply_rc reports '<Tool>: no changes' and the apply is skipped. run_rc (arc_meta_rc.py:194-195) appends the DRY-RUN line whenever apply is False, even with no changes. apply_page and apply_toolbox return or branch early instead. So the ending line is not a reliable 'would write' signal for the hover call alone.
fix: In run_rc, append the DRY-RUN line only when `not apply and changed` (`if not apply and changed: ... elif apply and changed: rewrite(...)`). Add a test in tests/arc/test_arc_meta_rc.py asserting that a no-change dry run's last line is the 'no changes' head.
In run_rc, append the DRY-RUN line only when `changed` (for example `if changed and not apply: ... elif changed: rewrite(...)`), matching run_toolbox's branch order.

minor.name: toolbox_members treats an empty content or rc dict as 'use the default'
minor.summary: `content or CONTENT` and `rc or RC` (lines 120-121) fall back to the demo values when a caller passes {}. A test that wants an empty rc or content object silently gets the full demo map, while the signature's Optional[...] = None suggests only None means default. Today callers pass empty members through `extra` instead, but the helper is a trap for the next test.
fix: Use `CONTENT if content is None else content` and `RC if rc is None else rc`.

minor.name: Redundant assertion before a stronger one
minor.summary: test_check_applied_keeps_a_plain_summary_hover_for_a_bold_summary asserts that ('hover_style_stale', None) is not among the codes and then that problems == []. The second assertion implies the first.
fix: Drop line 339, or keep it and make the final assertion carry the problems list as its message for diagnosis.

minor.name: Defaults-vs-schema test reports no reason on failure
minor.summary: test_defaults_validate_against_the_schema asserts `Draft202012Validator(schema).is_valid(defaults)` and never calls check_schema. The harness counterpart (tests/lib/test_config.py:405-410) checks the schema and calls validate, so a failure there names the offending path. Here a broken schema or a bad default fails as a bare 'assert False'.
fix: Call `jsonschema.Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)` and `jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(defaults)` instead of asserting is_valid.

minor.name: Format test module docstring omits its arc_meta_canonical half
minor.summary: The module docstring describes only the arc_meta_format generator (nested lists and Pro spacing). Lines 125-216 test arc_meta_canonical (rc_text, fields, load, add_dialog_ref, page), and a reader looking for canonical-builder tests would not expect them in this file.
fix: Extend the first docstring line to name arc_meta_canonical's readers and builders, or move lines 125-216 into a tests/arc/test_arc_meta_canonical.py.

minor.name: Process-history labels in test section headings and docstrings
minor.summary: Section headings and docstrings refer to how the work was produced, not to the behavior under test: '(SRC API tests 9-11)' in test_arc_meta_page.py:50, '--- ported ---' and '--- new ---' in test_arc_meta_toolbox.py:84,148, '--- rewrite: review fixes ---' in test_arc_meta_archive.py:173, and 'SRC wrote the rc ...' in test_arc_meta_rc.py:201. After the merge these labels mean nothing to a reader of the merged tree.
fix: Rename the headings after the behavior they group (e.g. '--- build_page / read_illustration ---', '--- run_toolbox: formatting and refusals ---', '--- rewrite: refusals and duplicates ---'), and reword the rc docstring as 'The rc is written as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark; ...'.

minor.name: Roundtrip before-check cannot see the stale illustration its docstring claims
minor.summary: The module docstring says each case starts with 'an illustration the page does not show'. The stale page is '<metadata/>', which has no <tool>, and _page_problems (plugins/arc-straps/skills/arc-meta/scripts/arc_meta_api.py:420-421) returns a single page_stale before any image comparison. So the before-assertion at line 41 never sees page_image_stale. The final set() check still catches a writer that drops the image, but the stated starting condition goes unobserved.
fix: In _stale_project, use a page that has a <tool> but no illustration (e.g. default_page(canonical)), and add ('page_image_stale', None) to the before-subset at line 41.

minor.name: Contract test imports the arc-meta generator at module load
minor.summary: test_root_separation.py imports arc._arc_toolbox at module level (line 22). That pulls in arc_meta_canonical and arc_meta_format at collection time. An import error in the arc-straps scripts then fails collection of the whole harness root-separation module, not just the 'arc-meta apply_rc' case and test_arc_meta_apply_lands_in_the_project.
fix: Move the arc._arc_toolbox import inside _arc_rc_args so only the arc cases depend on the arc-straps scripts being importable. Keep the module name spelled in source so tools/select_tests.py still selects the test.

minor.name: No-jsonschema plugins cases duplicated in two parametrizations
minor.summary: The cases {"plugins": {"Arc": {}}} and {"plugins": {"arc-straps": 3}} were added to test_minimal_validation_without_jsonschema (lines 164-165). They also run in test_plugins_rejects_bad_sections_without_jsonschema through BAD_PLUGINS (lines 190, 201-206), which checks a tighter 'plugins: ' message. The same input is tested twice, and the older parametrization uses the looser match.
fix: Revert the parametrize extension at lines 164-165 to the original two cases and leave the coverage to the BAD_PLUGINS test.

minor.name: Planning-time comment left in the plugins rejection test
minor.summary: The comment above test_plugins_rejects_bad_sections reads "Today's message reads '<root>: Additional properties ... plugins was unexpected'; the new one names the plugins path itself." It describes the error before this change. Once the change merges, the 'today' message is the new one, so the comment points the wrong way.
fix: Replace the two comment lines with one that states the contract, e.g. '# The error names the plugins path itself, not the root.'

minor.name: Docstring says 'the same folders' but the test checks only a subset
minor.summary: The docstring of test_default_pythonpath_mirrors_pyproject_and_the_pylint_hook says DEFAULT_PYTHONPATH, pytest's pythonpath and pylint's init-hook 'name the same folders'. The pyproject side is compared for equality, but the init-hook side only checks that each DEFAULT entry appears as a quoted substring. An extra folder in init-hook passes, so the test does not enforce the claim.
fix: Parse the list literal out of the init-hook (e.g. ast.literal_eval of the text after 'sys.path[:0] = ') and assert it equals list(sel.DEFAULT_PYTHONPATH).
Or reword the docstring to say the init-hook names every fallback root.
